CodeServerEditorDiagnostic.description: One editor diagnostic, 1-based line and column. `severity` is the narrowed vocabulary `diagnosticSeverityName` emits, not VS Code's numeric enum.

CodeServerNotifyResult.description: `kind` is the narrowed kind actually shown. An unrecognised kind reads as `info` rather than being dropped, so this echoes back what the user saw.

CodeServerOpenResult.description: The extension revealed `path`. `opened` is always true: a failure throws instead.

CodeServerRunInTerminalResult.description: `sent` reports that the text reached the terminal, not that the command succeeded: the extension host cannot read a terminal's output back. `terminal` is the reused terminal's name.

CodeServerSaveAllResult.description: A partial flush is reported rather than thrown, so `failed` names the files whose disk copy the caller must not trust.

CompanionEndpoints.description: Where else this host can be reached. `lanBaseUrl` is null on a loopback-bound server or a host with no routable interface; `tunnelBaseUrl` is null when no tunnel is running. `fingerprint` pins the self-signed certificate.

DetectedRuntimesReport.description: Which catalogued agent runtimes this Host already has. `resolution` is the only verdict here: `installed` means the command resolved and its catalogued `--version` was read, `missing` means it is on no PATH or install root, `package-runner` means it launches through npx and its presence cannot be established without a network install, `not-local` means the runtime has no local command at all. `versionOutput` is raw probe output; the version verdict is rendered by assessRuntimeVersion() in lib/ai/agent/external/runtime-version.ts.

HostCapabilityReport.description: What this host physically is, and which surfaces it can reach. `capabilities` is the append-only `CORE_CAPABILITY_IDS` vocabulary from lib/platform/capabilities.ts; an id a client does not recognise is a newer host, not an error.

HostFeatureLimits.description: Byte and count ceilings the host will actually enforce. Published so a client can refuse before the user commits, instead of after the host rejects.

HostFeatureManifest.description: The effective manifest: what this host offers THIS caller, already filtered by the caller's device grants. A client renders capability from this and never self-judges by command name. Deliberately open to extra properties: the manifest is versioned and additive, and a v1 host answering a v2 client must stay readable.

hostStateScope.description: The scope the host's own host-state actually lives under. A client that addresses host-state by its own pairing id asks for a namespace the host never wrote to, and every host_state_* call is refused with host_state_scope_mismatch.

HostRuntimeOperationDescriptor.description: One command the host declares it can actually serve right now. `healthy: false` with a `reason` is the honest answer a client renders as disabled-with-explanation, which is why an unhealthy operation is published rather than omitted.

HostStateActionReceipt.description: Per-action outcome. `duplicate` is a success (the idempotency key already landed), not a failure; `rejected` and `conflicted` carry the reason on `rejection`.

HostStateSnapshot.description: A cut of one host-state channel. `digest` and `cutHostSeq` are what a replica reconciles against; `state` is the channel's own payload, whose shape belongs to the channel.

HostStateStatus.description: `recovery` is load-bearing: while it is `recovering` nothing the host reports about a turn can be trusted, and `degraded` means recovery ran and failed rather than that state is fresh.

HostStateSubmitResponse.description: One receipt per submitted action, in submission order.

PiExtensionVerdict.description: Whether the bundled Cognia Pi extension on this Host is the one Cognia shipped. Pi ships no permission prompts of its own, so the extension that applies Cognia's matrix to its native read/edit/write/bash tools is a precondition for a session, not a diagnostic. Every refusing status is reported distinctly because "never shipped", "tampered" and "unpinned" are different sentences to whoever has to fix it.

WorkspaceRootsReport.description: Directories this Host will browse. `source` says why a root is allowed and therefore where it can be changed: `desktop-project` is registered by the active desktop project, `headless-workspaces-dir` is COGNIA_WORKSPACES_DIR and is fixed when the server starts.

SftpEntry.description: One entry on the remote machine. `size` is bytes, `modified` is the SFTP mtime in unix seconds and is absent when the server did not report one, and `permissions` is the raw mode word rather than a rendered string, because the client renders it and the server's own words are the only truth about it.

items.x-cognia-opaque-reason: The page envelope is the contract; the items are an existing domain collection whose compatibility remains owned by that domain.

nextPageToken.description: Opaque. Hand back unchanged as `pageToken` to read the next page; absent on the last page.

accepted.description: The host accepted the turn and runs it detached; the outcome arrives as member sub-session events.

RouterFusionOutcome.description: Router + Fusion's value envelope (ADR-0188): every outcome is a value, refusals included. `value` is the Run API answer the command names (RunCreated, RunSnapshotRead, RunEventsPage, RunSnapshot) or the reservation relay verdict; `error` carries the HTTP status and the contract code (403 ROUTER_FUSION_DISABLED while the companion switch is off).

ImportedWorkspaceHint.description:
A hint about a worktree found on disk that Registry did not create.

The planner records only the source root + execution root so callers can
insert a signed `WorkspaceRecord` with `owner_type = Imported` after
verifying paths.

Page_of_ResourceEvent.description:
One page of a collection.

Sparse rather than closed: `nextPageToken` is absent on the last page, and
that absence is the signal a client reads.

nextPageToken.description: Present exactly when another page exists.

Page_of_WorkspaceMaintenanceEvent.description:
One page of a collection.

Sparse rather than closed: `nextPageToken` is absent on the last page, and

nextPageToken.description: Present exactly when another page exists.

additions.description:
Added/deleted source lines in this hunk. Persisted as metrics only so
consumers can measure a partial apply without retaining patch text.

hunkIds.description: Empty means the whole file. Non-empty IDs select textual hunks.

appliedSelection.description:
Exact file/hunk selection used by the successful apply. An empty
selection means every file. `applied_selection_known` distinguishes
that from patch rows written before this field existed.

ReconcileOutcome.description:
Outcome of one reconcile pass. Callers persist the changes; the
planner itself does not mutate.

imported.description:
Worktrees on disk that Registry did not create. Callers store these
as `Imported` — they must never be auto-pruned.

orphaned.description:
Rows the Registry knew about but whose owner_ref no longer resolves
(session gone, task deleted, etc.). Callers should demote these to
`Restorable` or archive them.

reclaimed.description:
Rows the Registry already knew about and which passed signature
verification. Nothing changes for these.

mirrorPath.description: The bare mirror this checkout was derived from, and still fetches from.

resolvedRef.description:
The ref the requested base resolves to in this checkout, when the base
names one. `None` for a base that is only meaningful against a working
tree the caller has not created yet.

sourceRoot.description: The non-bare git root a bundle can now be acquired over.

WorkspaceBaseSpec.description:
The base ref a managed workspace was materialized against.

Interactive worktrees default to `WorkingState` (dirty local content is
carried into the isolated root). Background and scheduled Git tasks
default to `RemoteDefault` and refresh `origin/HEAD` at fire time.

oneOf.description: Snapshot of the current working tree, including uncommitted edits.
The current HEAD of the local branch.

`origin/HEAD` (or the configured default branch), refreshed at
acquisition.
A specific git ref (branch, tag, commit).
A pull request head that the Registry will fetch.

WorkspaceBundle.description:
A collection of `WorkspaceRootLease`s acquired atomically for one execution.

The Registry acquires a Bundle in one call; on failure it rolls back every
lease it already provisioned. See `bundle.rs` for the acquisition and
atomic-apply implementations.

WorkspaceBundleOutcome.description:
Outcome of a `WorkspaceBundle` apply. On compensation failure the bundle
ends up in `state = Conflict` and `conflicts` is non-empty.

WorkspaceBundleTurnLease.description: Persisted grouping for all TaskRuns opened for one Bundle turn.

WorkspaceEnvironmentAction.description: Server-authoritative actions that may be offered for an environment.

oneOf.description:
Reserved. `environment_actions` never emits `Review`, `Handoff` or
`Publish`, and `environment_actions_only_advertise_executable_lifecycle_and_git_operations`
pins that it must not: an inventory row is a directory, and reviewing or
handing off a *turn's* changes is the bundle handoff API's job, not this
one's. They stay in the vocabulary because the transport contract is
shared with that API. Adding one here without a producer would put a
button in the UI that nothing answers.

WorkspaceEnvironmentKind.description: Product lifecycle of a physical execution environment.

WorkspaceEnvironmentOwnership.description:
Product ownership of one row in the canonical workspace inventory.

This is intentionally distinct from [`WorkspaceOwnerType`]: it describes
which lifecycle controller owns the directory, not which product actor
requested it.

WorkspaceEnvironmentSummary.description:
Canonical inventory row joining Git's worktree porcelain with Registry
ownership. Callers must use `allowed_actions` rather than reimplementing
lifecycle policy in a UI or transport adapter.

lastUsedAt.description:
When the environment was last acquired, same provenance and same reason
as `size_bytes`. `None` for an unclaimed directory.

projectId.description:
Owning Workspace, so the inventory can be scoped to one project instead
of only ever being shown machine-wide. `None` for a directory found on
disk that no project claims.

sizeBytes.description:
On-disk size of the environment, when the Registry knows it.

Present on `WorkspaceRecord` since the registry shipped, and dropped by
this projection until now, which left the one surface that lists
worktrees unable to answer "what is actually taking up the disk". `None`
for a directory found on disk that no Registry row claims, and for a
managed row whose size has not been measured yet.

WorkspaceLifecyclePolicy.description: Retention policy inputs. All three knobs are user-adjustable in settings.

WorkspaceOwnerType.description:
Who created this managed workspace. Ownership determines whether the
Registry may prune or unlock the workspace during reconciliation.

`Imported` is reserved for worktrees discovered on disk that the Registry
cannot verify as its own — those rows never participate in auto-prune.

WorkspaceRecord.description:
One row in the Registry. Combines ownership, lifecycle, and the physical
isolation location.

`execution_root` is the on-disk path handed to executors. For Git
workspaces it is the worktree path; for `Shadow` it is the materialized
scratch directory. Trust is a separate axis and is not encoded here.

projectId.description:
Owning Workspace (the frontend `Project.id`), when it is known.

The crate addresses rows by path and `(owner_type, owner_ref)`, neither
of which can answer "which execution slots does this project own" —
several worktrees of one repository share a `git_common_dir`, and an
owner ref is a session or a team, never a project. Without it, deleting
a workspace cannot find the directories it produced and the inventory
can only be shown machine-wide.

Optional because the frontend owns the Project table: rows created
before this column, or found on disk with no matching project, stay
`None` and are classified `imported` — never auto-pruned (ADR-0111).

WorkspaceRootLease.description:
One logical root inside a Bundle, resolved to its physical execution
location.

`alias_path` is the path executors see. Multiple leases may point at the
same physical worktree when they share a Git common dir — the Bundle
composer collapses roots by `git_common_dir` before creating worktrees.

WorkspaceRootRole.description:
The role a logical root plays inside a Bundle.

Exactly one lease must be `Primary`; the rest are `Additional` (forwarded
as `additionalDirectories` when the executor spawns).

WorkspaceState.description:
Managed workspace lifecycle state. Transitions outside the Registry's
controlled paths are rejected fail-closed.

Legal transitions (all others error):

- `Provisioning → Active | Removing`
- `Active → Archived | Conflict | Removing`
- `Archived → Restorable | Removing`
- `Restorable → Active | Removing`
- `Conflict → Active | Removing`   (via `ConflictResolution`)
- `Removing → Removed`

`Removed` is terminal.

PinnedImage.description: A digest-pinned image as it travels in specs and catalog entries.

resolvedImage.description:
The image the declaration resolved to when approved. Absent for a
declaration that builds (ADR-0186), which carries `buildKey` instead.

CatalogImage.description:
The image a catalog entry names. Pinned except for a legacy entry derived
from a tag-only `COGNIA_RUNNER_IMAGE`, which admission refuses until the
tag is resolved to a digest.

tag.description: The tag a legacy entry was derived from; informational once pinned.

IsolationTier.description:
Isolation tiers, weakest first. `Ord` is the strength order, so
`max(a, b)` is the stricter of two requirements.

oneOf.description: A plain container: shared kernel, seccomp/pids/no-new-privileges.
A per-sandbox virtual machine (Kata, Firecracker, serverless pods).

createdAt.description:
Server-owned, and defaulted rather than required: the Host stamps both
on every write, and an operator authoring a baseline file by hand has
no timestamp to give. `0` reads as "not recorded", which is the honest
answer for a hand-written entry.

imageUser.description:
The image config's `USER`, read from the registry when the entry was
added. Absent means the image runs as root by default.

isolationFloor.description:
The weakest tier this image may run at. The effective floor is the
strictest of this, the tenant floor and the baseline floor.

provenance.description: Build key, commit and approval for a `build` entry.

sizeClassIds.description: Size classes this entry may run with; the first is the default.

CatalogEntryView.description: A catalog entry as a console reads it.

defaultEntry.description: True for the entry a project that names none gets.

effectiveFloor.description:
`max(entry floor, baseline floor, tenant floor)` — never lower than
what the entry itself declares.

retained.description: Older bundles a project may still pin, newest first.

CatalogRejection.description:
Why a stored tenant entry is not in the merged catalog.

A rejected entry stays stored and stays visible: an operator who added an
image the baseline allowlist later stopped permitting needs the reason,
not an entry that silently vanished.

GpuRequest.description: Reserved for GPU sandboxes; never admitted today.

OfferedBundle.description:
An agent bundle a deployment offers (ADR-0183): where a driver pulls it
from, and the digest and release tag a spec records. The spec itself does
not carry the registry, so a bundle moving registries between releases does
not change any spec digest.

SizeClass.description:
A size class. `gpu` is reserved and dormant: the type accepts it so the
model does not have to change when GPU sandboxes land, and admission
refuses any class that sets it (`gpu_not_supported`).

gpu.description: Reserved; dormant. See the type doc.

volumeMib.description: Persistent workspace volume size for persistent sandboxes.

DeclarationRead.description:
One declaration file, as bytes plus the digest of those bytes.

Deliberately *not* parsed here. The devcontainer and workspace-config
grammars, their closed-world refusals and the RFC 8785 declaration digest
live in one place — `lib/project-environment` — and a second
implementation in Rust would be a parity liability with nothing to gain:
this Host's job on this path is access to a checkout the approver's
browser cannot reach. The digest over the raw bytes is what makes "the
file changed since you looked at it" answerable without parsing either
grammar.

bytesSha256.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the exact bytes above.

path.description: Absolute path of the file that was read.

relativePath.description: Repository-relative path, which is what an approval record stores.

OfferedBundleView.description:
An offered agent bundle, for a console that must show which digest a
sandbox would inject and which older ones a project may still pin.

current.description: True for the current bundle, false for a retained older one.

EgressTier.description:
Egress posture. The wire value for "open" is `on`, the value
`ProjectEnvironmentPolicy.network` already persists.

Platform.description: A platform the environment plane can run. Only `linux` images run.

ProbeCacheView.description:
The cached probe verdict for one (user image, bundle) pair.

A view over what the driver stored, not a second source of truth: these
are the fields a console shows. The entry is parsed by
`cognia_sandbox_pool::probe_cache::ProbeCacheEntry`, the same type the
driver writes it with, so the two cannot disagree about its shape.

problems.description: Empty when the probe accepted the image.

requestedUser.description: The user the probe was asked about: a name, a uid, or `uid:gid`.

resolvedUser.description:
The user the agent actually runs as, as the image resolved it. Absent
when the requested user does not exist in the image.

runtimes.description: Bundle runtimes this image's C library can run.

workspaceOwner.description: Who owned the workspace when the probe ran.

name.description: Absent for a numeric uid the image has no passwd entry for.

remappedFrom.description:
The declared user's own ids, when it was remapped onto the workspace
owner.

bot_delivery_replay.description: `replayed` is false when the row was no longer dead-lettered, which is what a duplicated request produces.

bot_run_manual.description: `created` is false when the idempotency key matched an existing delivery, i.e. this was a retry replay rather than a second run.

bot_trigger_set_armed.description: The value the host settled on. Echoed back so a client can reconcile its optimistic flip.

connector_enqueue_outbound.description: What the host did with the relayed reply (ADR-0131). `reused` is true when the idempotency key matched an existing job — i.e. this was a retry replay, not a second send.

connectors_onebot_probe.description: Reverse-WS OneBot clients currently dialed in to the in-app server.

sftp_list_dir.description: One directory on the remote machine. `.` and `..` are dropped where they are read, so this is entries only.

sftp_stat.description: One entry on the remote machine.

sftp_realpath.description: The path as the remote machine resolves it, symlinks included. The one place a client learns where a relative path actually lands.

sftp_create_dir.description: The remote machine accepted the change. There is nothing else to report: a failure arrives as an error envelope carrying the server's own words.

sftp_rename_entry.description: The remote machine accepted the change. There is nothing else to report: a failure arrives as an error envelope carrying the server's own words.

sftp_delete_entry.description: The remote machine accepted the change. There is nothing else to report: a failure arrives as an error envelope carrying the server's own words.

sftp_download_open.description: An approved download. `chunkBytes` is what the host will serve per read, negotiated here rather than assumed by the client, and `size` is what the remote machine reported at open.

sftp_download_read_chunk.description: One chunk of the file, base64 encoded. `eof` is true when the server returned fewer bytes than asked for, which is how a read loop stops. A short read mid-file is legal SFTP and the host loops over it, so a short answer here really is the end.

sftp_download_close.description: The handle is gone. Closing one that already expired reports the same thing, because the caller's intent is satisfied either way.

sftp_upload_open.description: An approved upload. `writeHead` is where the host will start writing, taken from what is already on the remote machine rather than from the client's memory of what it sent.

sftp_upload_write_chunk.description: The host's write head after this chunk, which is where the next one goes and where a resume starts. The client never names an offset the host did not reach.

sftp_upload_commit.description: What is actually on the remote machine now. `size` is re-read from the machine rather than reported from the write head, so a file something else also wrote is described truthfully. `complete` is that size measured against what the client declared at open.

sftp_upload_abort.description: The handle is gone. The partial file is deliberately left where it is: removing it would be a delete nobody asked for, and those bytes are what a later resume starts from.

sftp_session_close.description: How many pooled connections for that profile were dropped. Zero is the ordinary answer when nothing was open.

execution_run_detail.description: Selected run summary, non-private journal, exact approval artifacts and optional completed Bot result. Read is scoped to the active account and agent.run capability.

bot_installation_mutate.description: Authoritative installation projection or idempotent removal receipt; no auth-session handles.

bot_console_read.description: Host Bot console catalog, configuration rows or sanitized credential choices.

resolvedImage.description:
The image the declaration resolved to when approved. Absent for a
declaration that builds (ADR-0186), which carries `buildKey` instead.

environment_approval_list.description:
One page of a collection.

Sparse rather than closed: `nextPageToken` is absent on the last page, and
that absence is the signal a client reads.

nextPageToken.description: Present exactly when another page exists.

environment_declaration_read.description:
Every declaration file a repository has, plus where the Host looked.

**All** of them, not the first one that matched. Precedence between
`.cognia/workspace.json` and a devcontainer file is decided by
`lib/project-environment/read-environment-declaration.ts`, together with
the trust gate and the parse — and a Host that returned only its own first
match would be a second, silent answer to the same question. Returning the
set keeps that rule in one place and still costs one round trip.

files.description:
In `DECLARATION_FILES` order; empty when the repository declares nothing,
which is the common case and not an error.

searched.description:
Every path that was looked for, so a caller can say where it looked
instead of only "not found".

environment_driver_status.description: The driver's own answer about itself.

availableTiers.description:
Empty with `reachable: false`. An unreachable daemon attests no tier,
which is not the same claim as attesting none.

A project's permission to use egress beyond the presets: extra domains on
the allowlist tier, or the open tier.

image, the manifest digest otherwise. This is what a catalog entry pins.

platforms.description: In the order the caller asked for them.

unreadable.description:
True when an entry exists but this build cannot read its shape. "No

A dry run of admission: what this Host would give the spec, or why it
would refuse. Never starts anything.

availableTiers.description: The tiers the driver could attest when this ran.

fault.description:
Whether the refusal was a fault (infrastructure) rather than an answer
about the spec. A fault falls back at spawn time unless isolation is
mandatory, so a preview must not report one as a verdict on the spec.
